free_parameters.name: target_avg_bits
free_parameters.why: witness only fixes args.target_avg_bits is not None; 4.5 is inside [base_bits=4, upgrade_bits=5] so the Mode-A guard on the path prefix holds, and it makes both the downgrade and upgrade candidate sets non-empty.

free_parameters.name: base_bits
free_parameters.why: code default for the Mode-A budget range; unchanged.

free_parameters.name: upgrade_bits
free_parameters.why: code default for the Mode-A budget range; unchanged.

free_parameters.name: model_config
free_parameters.why: small but real locally saved HF GPT-2 checkpoint (same recipe as tests/conftest.py tiny_gpt2); the target decision only tests the boolean args.downgrade, so architecture and width cannot change it. No network or GPU is used.

free_parameters.name: sensitivity_rows
free_parameters.value: one row per contiguous 8-output-channel window of every quantizable layer, delta_ppl spread deterministically over [-1.0, -0.1]
free_parameters.why: real rows derived from the constructed checkpoint via flexposit.utils.quantizable_layers so main()'s valid-layer filter keeps them; the target line only reads args.downgrade, not any delta_ppl value.

free_parameters.name: seed
free_parameters.why: torch.manual_seed(0) before constructing weights makes the checkpoint byte-identical across runs; the target decision does not depend on the weights.

free_parameters.name: dtype
free_parameters.why: both the FP32 reference and probe checkpoint are tiny CPU models; the target is reached before any eval or quantization, and fp32 avoids fp16 CPU loading caveats.

free_parameters.name: dry_run
free_parameters.why: main() exits right after the plan is printed, so no model quantization, WikiText download, or GPU work happens below the target line.

free_parameters.name: downgrade_nsize
free_parameters.why: left at the code default (None), which resolves to int(base_bits) inside the positive branch.

execution.entry_reason: Static analysis reports call_chain_status=not_found: the declared first node flexposit.api.quantize is a separate Python API implementation that never calls flexposit.mpq.channel_window.main. The target is inside the argparse CLI main, which is only reachable by running that module. The driver therefore calls the deepest chain node, channel_window.main, directly with sys.argv built from the witness inputs; main's own function and all code on the path to line 571 are the real pinned repository code.
